answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a reputation kernel that only grows through verifiable work, never through registration. Fresh identities start at zero and must cross a minimum standing horizon before they can earn, so mass clones gain nothing instantly. Each output carries a weighted proof of compute binding the task to the author, making ferrous copying of identical responses detectable and cheap to penalize. A one-time non-transferable stake that slashes on proven cloning raises the cost of running many puppets above any reward they could capture.
